from ortools.sat.python import cp_model

n = 27
fixed = {
    9: 23,
    12: 13,
    18: 1,
    21: 21,
    26: 14,
}

model = cp_model.CpModel()

# q[i] is the column of the queen in row i
q = [model.NewIntVar(0, n-1, f'q{i}') for i in range(n)]

# Apply fixed assignments
for row, col in fixed.items():
    model.Add(q[row] == col)

# All different columns
model.AddAllDifferent(q)

# Diagonal constraints: q[i] - q[j] != i - j and q[i] - q[j] != j - i
# This means q[i] + i != q[j] + j and q[i] - i != q[j] - j
# We can use all-different on q[i] + i and q[i] - i

# Create auxiliary variables for diagonals
diag1 = [model.NewIntVar(-n+1, 2*n-2, f'd1_{i}') for i in range(n)]  # q[i] - i
diag2 = [model.NewIntVar(0, 2*n-2, f'd2_{i}') for i in range(n)]     # q[i] + i

for i in range(n):
    model.Add(diag1[i] == q[i] - i)
    model.Add(diag2[i] == q[i] + i)

model.AddAllDifferent(diag1)
model.AddAllDifferent(diag2)

solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
solver.parameters.max_time_in_seconds = 30.0
solver.parameters.num_search_workers = 8

result = solver.Solve(model)
print(f"Result: {result}")
print(f"Status: {solver.StatusName(result)}")

if result == cp_model.OPTIMAL or result == cp_model.FEASIBLE:
    solution = [solver.Value(q[i]) for i in range(n)]
    print(f"Solution: {solution}")
    
    # Verify
    cols = set()
    d1s = set()
    d2s = set()
    valid = True
    for i in range(n):
        col = solution[i]
        d1 = col - i
        d2 = col + i
        if col in cols or d1 in d1s or d2 in d2s:
            valid = False
            print(f"Conflict at row {i}, col {col}")
            break
        cols.add(col)
        d1s.add(d1)
        d2s.add(d2)
    
    # Check fixed assignments
    for row, col in fixed.items():
        if solution[row] != col:
            print(f"Fixed assignment violated: q[{row}] = {solution[row]}, expected {col}")
            valid = False
    
    print(f"Valid: {valid}")
else:
    print("No solution found")

def solve_n_queens(n, fixed):
    # available_cols[i] = set of available columns for row i
    # But actually, each column can only be used once
    # So we track: used columns, used diag1 (col - row), used diag2 (col + row)
    
    solution = [None] * n
    used_cols = set()
    used_diag1 = set()  # col - row
    used_diag2 = set()  # col + row
    
    # Apply fixed assignments first
    for row, col in fixed.items():
        d1 = col - row
        d2 = col + row
        if col in used_cols or d1 in used_diag1 or d2 in used_diag2:
            return None  # Fixed assignments conflict
        solution[row] = col
        used_cols.add(col)
        used_diag1.add(d1)
        used_diag2.add(d2)
    
    # Order rows by fewest available options (MRV heuristic)
    def get_available(row):
        avail = []
        for col in range(n):
            if col in used_cols:
                continue
            d1 = col - row
            d2 = col + row
            if d1 in used_diag1 or d2 in used_diag2:
                continue
            avail.append(col)
        return avail
    
    # Precompute which rows are fixed
    fixed_rows = set(fixed.keys())
    
    def backtrack(remaining_rows):
        if not remaining_rows:
            return True
        
        # Find row with minimum remaining values
        best_row = None
        best_avail = None
        best_count = n + 1
        
        for row in remaining_rows:
            avail = get_available(row)
            count = len(avail)
            if count == 0:
                return False
            if count < best_count:
                best_count = count
                best_row = row
                best_avail = avail
                if count == 1:
                    break
        
        if best_row is None:
            return True
        
        remaining = remaining_rows - {best_row}
        
        for col in best_avail:
            d1 = col - best_row
            d2 = col + best_row
            
            solution[best_row] = col
            used_cols.add(col)
            used_diag1.add(d1)
            used_diag2.add(d2)
            
            if backtrack(remaining):
                return True
            
            solution[best_row] = None
            used_cols.remove(col)
            used_diag1.remove(d1)
            used_diag2.remove(d2)
        
        return False
    
    remaining = set(range(n)) - fixed_rows
    if backtrack(remaining):
        return solution
    return None
